findings: Entry delay destroys the edge: entering at the first real>=1.2 SOL sample averages +0.62% per trade (win 45%), entering 100 slots late averages -3.6% (win 28%), 900 slots late -4.4% (win 14%).
Later entries are worse even at zero delay: first real>=1.2 averages +0.62%, >=3 SOL -0.57%, >=5 SOL -1.51%, >=10 SOL -2.06%.
Ladder/trailing exits hurt: all-out +10% beats TP ladder + trailing on this window (median coin ends -17% from its early price).
Pyramids sized by real reserves help: SOL-denominated screen total +0.13 SOL with 0 adds, +0.74 with 1, +0.88 with 2, +0.97 with 3; live grade confirms (adds=1 graded -0.70 vs adds=3 at -0.38).

92% of mints that reach 1 SOL real reserves run at least +10% soon after; 31% run +100%; median max return +60% within 30k slots — but the 5-position cap and 1%-of-real-reserve order cap keep early sizes near 0.011 SOL, so the edge converts to little absolute PnL.

honest_assessment: Dev return -0.038 is far below the top-3 cutoff (~1.29) with no concrete fixable cause left: the entry is gross-profitable (+1.52 SOL over 391 round trips) but fees (1.90 SOL, ~2.5% curve per round trip plus fixed tx fees) eat it, and 19 of 20 stress copies lose money, so the dev score leans on this window's coins. The top-3 dev entries (+129% to +176%) likely use a different mechanism (holder/tape/overhang selection signals this bot does not have) or are overfit to the dev window; chasing 1.29 with fitted parameters would not generalize to the unseen final window. This entry meets the guardrails, is fully deterministic, and is the best honest version of the early-crossing model class — but it is NOT in the prize zone and should be submitted only as a counting entry if the coordinator judges that worthwhile.

Self-critique by instrumented debug runs found and fixed three real bugs (see version_history): a zeroed size cap, a gain-gated time stop that stranded positions, and a pending-sell flag that blocked retries after max_slippage rejections.
strategy: Deterministic early-crossing breakout + positive pyramid. Enter a mint within ~120 slots of its real reserves first crossing 1.2 SOL (max order 1% of real reserves, ~0.011 SOL first buy). Add up to 3 times at +5% on blended cost, sized by current real reserves (up to 0.45 SOL). Exit all out at +10%, hard stop -5%, unconditional time stop 1200 slots. Drawdown governor halts entries past -8% and flattens past -15%. Buy slippage 400bps, sell slippage 2000bps. No clocks, no unseeded randomness, sorted iteration everywhere.

v2 early-crossing (real>=1.2, TP +10% all-out, SL -5%): net PnL -0.78 SOL, 224 fills, 67 coins, win 24.7%, guardrails met.
v3 pending-position tracking + buy slippage 400bps + no EMA entry filter: net PnL -0.78 SOL, 706 fills, 111 coins, win 15.2%, 126 rejected (96 sells insufficient_tokens from duplicate sells).

v4 freshness window 900 -> 120 slots + pending-sell tracking: net PnL -0.24 SOL, 88 fills, 36 coins, win 17.9%. Debug found 5 positions stuck all run: their sells were rejected for max_slippage and pendingSells blocked retries forever; also a gain-gated time stop let frozen prices sit in the +5%..+10% band.

v5 sell slippage 800 -> 2000bps + clear pending flags on rejected/failed fills + unconditional time stop: net PnL -0.38 SOL, 1033 fills, 369 coins, 391 round trips, win 19.7%, gross +1.52 SOL, fees -1.90 SOL. Best honest version; shipped.
v5b buy slippage 1500bps: net PnL -0.38 SOL, no improvement; reverted to 400bps.
v6 pyramids 3 -> 1 add: net PnL -0.70 SOL, worse; reverted to 3 adds.
